templates.stem_template: You made the last {N} commits by mistake on `main`. Undo them but keep all changes staged.
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "for i in $(seq 1 {total_commits}); do echo \"content $i\" > file$i.txt && git add file$i.txt && git commit -m \"commit $i\"; done"]
templates.explanation_template: `git reset --soft HEAD~{N}` moves HEAD back {N} commits without touching the index or working tree, so all changes from those commits remain staged. `--hard` would destroy the changes, and `--mixed` would unstage them.

templates.stem_template: You want to rename the local branch `{old_name}` to `{new_name}` without switching to it. Which command does this?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'initial' > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -m 'initial commit'", "git branch {old_name}", "echo 'feature' > feature.txt && git add feature.txt && git commit -m 'add feature'"]
templates.explanation_template: `git branch -m <old> <new>` renames a branch without checking it out. Swapping the arguments renames in the wrong direction. `rename-branch` and `--rename` are not valid Git commands.

templates.stem_template: After rebasing `feature` onto `main`, how many total commits are reachable from `feature`? (Count the initial base commit.)
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'base' > base.txt && git add base.txt && git commit -m 'base'", "git checkout -b feature", "for i in $(seq 1 {feature_commits}); do echo \"feat $i\" > feat$i.txt && git add feat$i.txt && git commit -m \"feature $i\"; done", "git checkout main", "for i in $(seq 1 {main_commits}); do echo \"main $i\" > main$i.txt && git add main$i.txt && git commit -m \"main $i\"; done", "git checkout feature", "git rebase main"]

templates.stem_template: You have multiple stashes saved. You want to apply the stash at index {stash_idx} without dropping it from the list. Which command do you run?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'base' > app.js && git add app.js && git commit -m 'initial'", "echo 'stash2' > f2.txt && git add f2.txt && git stash push -m 'stash2'", "echo 'stash1' > f1.txt && git add f1.txt && git stash push -m 'stash1'", "echo 'stash0' > f0.txt && git add f0.txt && git stash push -m 'stash0'"]
templates.explanation_template: `git stash apply <index>` reapplies the changes recorded at stash index without removing the stash entry from the stash stack.

templates.stem_template: You need to copy only the commit on `{feat_branch}` onto `main`. Which command applies this single commit?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'v1' > main.py && git add main.py && git commit -m 'initial'", "git checkout -b {feat_branch}", "echo 'wip' > wip.py && git add wip.py && git commit -m 'wip feature'", "echo 'fix' > hotfix.py && git add hotfix.py && git commit -m 'patch'", "git checkout main"]
templates.explanation_template: `git cherry-pick <branch>` applies changes from a specific branch's commit directly onto the current HEAD without merging branch histories.

templates.stem_template: During a merge conflict on `{target_file}`, you decide to resolve it by keeping the incoming version from the branch being merged. Which command selects the incoming version for `{target_file}`?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'base' > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -m 'initial'", "git checkout -b feature", "echo 'incoming' > {target_file} && git add {target_file} && git commit -m 'feature commit'", "git checkout main", "echo 'current' > {target_file} && git add {target_file} && git commit -m 'main commit'", "git merge feature || true"]
templates.explanation_template: `git checkout --theirs <file>` checks out the incoming version of a conflicting file during a merge conflict.

templates.stem_template: You accidentally staged `{target_file}` with `git add`. You want to unstage it while keeping your working copy intact. Which command accomplishes this?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'initial' > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -m 'initial'", "echo 'secret data' > {target_file} && git add {target_file}"]
templates.explanation_template: `git restore --staged <file>` removes the specified file from the staging index without modifying the copy in the working directory.

templates.stem_template: You noticed an issue on public `main` and want to safely invert commit HEAD~{N} with a new commit. Which command should you run?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "for i in $(seq 1 5); do echo \"c$i\" > f$i.txt && git add f$i.txt && git commit -m \"commit $i\"; done"]
templates.explanation_template: `git revert HEAD~K` creates a new commit that records the exact inverse of HEAD~K, safely undoing changes on shared branches without rewriting history.

templates.stem_template: You want to create an annotated tag named `{tag_name}` with the message "{release_note}". Which command creates an annotated tag?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "echo 'code' > app.py && git add app.py && git commit -m 'release build'"]
templates.explanation_template: `git tag -a <tag> -m <msg>` creates an annotated Git tag containing full author metadata, date, and message.

templates.stem_template: You want to inspect the commit history compactly on one line per commit, limited to the last {max_count} commits. Which command does this?
templates.setup_commands: ["git init", "for i in $(seq 1 10); do echo \"c$i\" > f$i.txt && git add f$i.txt && git commit -m \"commit $i\"; done"]
templates.explanation_template: `git log --oneline -n {max_count}` formats the commit log into one condensed line per commit and limits output to {max_count} entries.
